name: pocket88k
note: The layout of the s5 images (the new firmware with the song engine: fwbuild.json's s5 variants, built with FW_S5). IROM, the cart MCU's code memory, is 88 KB, the size chosen for the FPGA fit of these images (B Jam's decision of 2026-10-21): rom0 32 KB + a 56 KB extension (7 slices of 8 KB). Everything else is as pocket72k (the brain hole 0x5360-0xD2EB unchanged, WRAM, the MCU's working RAM, 48 KB in the 0.3.0 map). Only the s5 variants of fwbuild.json link it (the test benches' images and the size report: no bitstream carries it yet). Generated into pocket88k.ld by tools/mkld.py.

regions.name: brain
regions.what: CPU MATE brain (brain.bin, 32,652 B, linked for 0x5360; jump table + text + its rodata)

regions.name: brain_data
regions.what: buddy data fixed by the brain link: cap 1 KB, CM 0x1C20, T16 0x2020, key/CM_BAD/counters, movem shadow, brain RAM 2 KB at 0x22C0

regions.name: wram_sched
regions.what: NOT cleared by crt0: the 0.2.6 relocated lists (.bss_noclear); in 0.3.0 the scheduler state / timer wheel

regions.name: wcode
regions.what: write-locked code window, bitstream-initialised: cf.bin at 0x2C00, 64 zero bytes, image tables 0x4110-0x4647, then the glue's code and rodata

regions.name: wram_upper
regions.what: 0.3.0 upper data: synth state, scaling buffers, extra .bss (.bss_upper, cleared by the s1 crt0), WRAM-ROM spill, boot overlay at power-on

regions.name: stack
regions.what: stack, 5,120 B as in 0.2.6 (static bound with F5's 4 KB local buffer: 4,960 B)

sram.cold_note: the cold part: the A858 screen and the cart program's text, which the MegaWire task reaches with no module only through the screen; its own CRC-32 is checked with the hot part's by the thread's first work after the 68000's release, and a cold part that fails leaves the task running and the screen uncalled (a check of the whole image before the release held the 68000 past the VDP's first VS)

sram_note: MegaWire (docs/MCU_INTERFACE.md section 3.7): the SRAM image, carried in the Little-Man Firmware file and copied into SRAM by the core's boot stub (its 64-byte header at 0x08000000, board/pocket/s3_sram.c; then the MegaWire code and rodata, run in place) and the MegaWire RAM (.sram_bss) at 0x08018C00, after CPU MATE's rate hash 0x08018000-0x08018BFF (buddy/buddy.h). Builds without these objects link nothing there (the scheduler probes).
irom_hi_text_note: the four boot-time / out-of-line functions 0.2.6 already placed after the brain (in the 0.2.6 build's relocation list); everything else of .text stays in irom_lo. Move whole input sections here when .text outgrows irom_lo. From 2026-10-11: the objects only the s1 images have (the new firmware, built with FW_S1) of the core dispatcher, the boot and the interim bodies (no 0.2.6 object has these names, so the milestone-2 images do not move); same IROM, same fetch cost. Later s1 work added the watchdog, fatal halt, MCU reset, TEST counters, debug save and interim audio objects. A review of the split (measured: irom_lo 2,716 / irom_hi 2,092 B free in TEST, 5,828 / 5,328 in RELEASE) moved nothing (docs/LAYOUT.md, the s1 images). On 2026-10-19 the F5 copy (f5_s1.c, 912 B) went back to irom_lo, which the move of the s1 SFX code to the code window had left with 1.8 KB while irom_hi had 52 B (TEST, measured). In pocket88k: the song engine's objects (core/song, the s5 glue) go after the brain, where the 56 KB extension has the room; irom_lo keeps the s1 split. Test build 5 on: the boot cache's IROM stub (boot/boot_cache.c, crt0 calls it once a boot) goes after the brain too; the debug save (dbgsave.c) moves to the code window in this layout (wcode_text).
wcode_text_note: s1 objects placed in the code window after the glue (no 0.2.6 object has these names, so the milestone images do not move). From 2026-10-19: our code for the chip's SFX channels (interim/s1/sfx_s1.c: a D1 / D2 / D3 post, the synth tick, a pending start), 4.5 KB that the TEST IROM no longer holds (212 + 168 B free before); the window keeps its fixed bytes (cf.bin, pad, tables) first. From 2026-10-23 (test build 5): test build 4b's TEST record writer of the boot cache (s1_cache4b.c, as in pocket72k) and the TEST debug save (dbgsave.c, version 9; RELEASE builds its three empty functions) in the window, so that the TEST IROM keeps room for the boot cache's stub, the s5 glue's TEST counts and the check crt0 makes in the s5 images, and C6's code stays in irom_lo, where its timing was measured.
upper_bss_objects_note: the song engine's state (S + 26 voices, G, SFX, the SFX and BGM tables, the Z80 queue, the packet staging; the ordered queue) goes to wram_upper, where the 0.3.0 plan budgets it (+~6.3 KB), not to wram_data (6 KB, the hot .data/.bss)
sched_noclear_note: the same five .bss objects 0.2.6 relocated to the gap 0x2AC0-0x2BFF (their initial contents are never read; this was argued variable by variable when 0.2.6 placed them). Not cleared by crt0. From 2026-10-27: the sprite engine's flush list (core/sprite spr_posts.c, 64 B; every entry the flush reads is written by spr_load_list first, so its start contents are never read) takes part of the room the 0.2.6 engine's two lists left (TEST's wram_data holds the engine's state).
